digest.scope: Finite-candidate contextual bandit, one action per prompt; not autoregressive token-level PPO or a trained LLM
digest.label_source: Python applies fixed rankings written by the course author; not a human-rater study
digest.candidate_source: All answer texts, including sums, are calculated by Python before training

sft.demonstration_mode: number only; new explain/missing requirements enter via preference data
sft.label_smoothing_reason: retain exploration probability in this four-action teaching environment

reward.normalization: subtract per-context candidate mean, divide by training candidate-score standard deviation

ppo.advantage: sampled normalized RM reward minus pre-update learned value; no multi-token GAE
ppo.reference_kl: exact KL(policy || fixed SFT), optimized separately from reward surrogate
ppo.value_target: normalized RM score only; the explicit analytic KL term is not part of this critic target

comparison_limits: Same SFT policy state and same train family/preference pool; equal policy update counts do not equal compute, data, or statistical budgets.
PPO includes reward-model training and a learned critic and samples current actions; DPO reuses offline labeled pairs.
The preference pool adds new task conditions not present in SFT demonstrations; this is not evidence that PPO or DPO beats SFT on equivalent data.
Candidate meanings are fixed and structured features directly expose task conditions. No Chinese comprehension, calculation, open-ended response generation, or broad safety conclusion.
One fixed seed and one small family split; validation/test are evaluated only after training decisions are fixed.
No deliberate learned-RM exploitation result is asserted; independent rule checks are reported whether or not RM disagrees.
